summary:
CONFIRMED UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS on web-01 to the shared 'deploy' account. From 2026-11-08 07:00 to 2026-11-12 14:20 UTC, about 60 successful password logins to 'deploy' came from 54.36.199.108 (an address that is not in the staff directory, and not the CI host at 10.20.0.30). Each login started a command session, then closed. The deploy account is supposed to be key-only, used only by CI from 10.20.0.30, so the password was stolen or guessed somewhere. Logs do not show what the commands were. Since the restart at 17:03 UTC, deploy has also had failed password guesses from 193.163.146.66 and 71.6.37.144 (no success). 71.6.37.144 also sent POST /xmlrpc.php. Maria's own logins to deploy from 73.162.171.242, 96.255.6.208 and 100.37.236.110 look legitimate (they match her other keys and addresses), but she should confirm.

WHAT I CHANGED (web-01):
- Locked the deploy password and rotated it (rotate-secret deploy-password). The new password goes to the staff vault and the help desk. Maria can still get in with her own key and sudo.
- sshd: added a Match User deploy block with PasswordAuthentication no, so deploy is key-only from any address. The CI key line in deploy's authorized_keys is now pinned with from="10.20.0.30".
- Removed the sudo rule that let deploy run /usr/bin/rsync as root (a root escape for anyone holding the deploy password). CI's release only uses larkspur-deploy and is unaffected. Backup of the old sudoers file is in /root.
- Rotated app-db-password (rotate-secret). deploy could read wp-config.php, so the site DB password was exposed to the intruder. I updated /etc/larkspur/report.cnf (a second copy the tool does not know about). The report, orders and payouts jobs all run OK afterwards.
- Verified: CI release every 3 min still ok (17:09 ok), payouts ok, orders and report ok.

WHAT I DID NOT CHANGE, AND WHY:
- payment-key: not rotated. The intruder only had the deploy account. payments.ini is root-only and deploy cannot read it, and no sudo log shows deploy running anything beyond larkspur-deploy. There is no evidence the key was read, so I did not rotate it (that would break payouts).
- Logs do not show whether the intruder ran commands beyond the sessions, so the web-01 root state is not fully certain. Recommended: review /var/log/auth.log and the nginx log for 54.36.199.108 between Nov 8 and Nov 12, and check whether any other secrets were on the host's readable paths.
- db-01 and ci-01: no compromise found. Logins came from the expected staff addresses and the backup/CI hosts. db-01 bind addresses are fine (MariaDB on 3306 is office-network only per config review; redis is localhost-only). ci-01 repo HEAD (883881f) matches what is deployed.

OPEN ITEMS FOR MARIA (not fixed):
- web-01 still allows password logins for staff in general (needed for lucia, dana, jcole, hgrant, pshah, mfischer). Recommend moving staff to keys.
- Grafana listens on 0.0.0.0:3000 on web-01. Restrict it to the office network or VPN.
- /var/www/larkspur/wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/availability.php is untracked (hand-copied in April, served to the booking box). Looks benign, but should be committed or removed.
- Backup copies of the old sudoers file and deploy authorized_keys are in /root on web-01.

UPDATE (final). Confirmed unauthorized access on web-01 to the shared 'deploy' account: about 60 successful password logins from 54.36.199.108 between 2026-11-08 07:00 and 2026-11-12 14:20 UTC, each starting a command session. Logs do not show what was run. This address is not in the staff directory. The release and the CI key are separate and were not affected.

CONTAINED on web-01: deploy password locked and rotated; deploy is key-only (sshd Match block) and its CI key is pinned to from="10.20.0.30"; the sudo rule letting deploy run /usr/bin/rsync as root was removed; app-db-password rotated, with /etc/larkspur/report.cnf updated to match (report, orders and payouts jobs verified); unlisted account 'jpark' (not in staff.txt, no keys, no logins seen) locked and set to nologin. CI release (every 3 min), maintenance, db dump and payouts all verified running after the changes.

NOT CHANGED: payment key (no evidence it was read: deploy cannot read payments.ini, which is root-only, and no sudo activity by deploy beyond larkspur-deploy is logged). Rotating it would break payouts. Also not changed: web-01 still allows password SSH logins for staff, and Grafana listens on all addresses on port 3000. Both are open risks.

ONGOING: internet password guessing against web-01 SSH continues (61.177.48.155, 218.92.195.201, 24.118.35.99, 45.155.183.109, 198.235.155.206 and others, usernames like ubuntu/test/mysql/dev). None succeeded. Note: hgrant had successful password logins from 108.21.194.27 at 17:09-17:10 UTC; this address is also used by pshah and jcole and looks like a legitimate home network, but Maria should confirm with Hollis.

db-01 and ci-01: no compromise found; logins match staff and service addresses; repo HEAD matches the deployed release. Recommend: review web-01 auth and nginx logs for 54.36.199.108 for Nov 8 to Nov 12; move staff to SSH keys and restrict password SSH; restrict Grafana to office/VPN; commit or remove the untracked inc/availability.php in the plugin.

UPDATE. Unauthorized access on web-01 to the shared 'deploy' account: about 60 successful password logins from 54.36.199.108 between 2026-11-08 07:00 and 2026-11-12 14:20 UTC, each starting a command session. The logs do not show what was run. Containment is holding: after the change at about 17:09 UTC, 54.36.199.108 made one more attempt at 17:11:53 and it was rejected before authentication (deploy is now key-only and the CI key is pinned to 10.20.0.30). No successful logins from that address after the change.

Changes on web-01: deploy password locked and rotated; deploy key-only with CI key pinned to from="10.20.0.30"; sudo rule letting deploy run /usr/bin/rsync as root removed; app-db-password rotated and /etc/larkspur/report.cnf updated to match (report, orders and payouts verified); unlisted account jpark (not in staff.txt, no keys, no logins seen) locked and set to nologin.

Verified after the changes: CI release every 3 minutes (last ok at 17:09), payouts ok, database dump ok at 17:10, maintenance ok.

Not changed: payment key (no evidence it was read; deploy cannot read payments.ini, which is root-only; rotating would break payouts). web-01 still accepts SSH passwords from the internet, and internet password guessing continues (none succeeded). Grafana listens on all addresses on port 3000.

Please confirm: Maria's own deploy logins from 73.162.171.242 / 96.255.6.208 / 100.37.236.110 earlier (they look legitimate); hgrant and jcole password logins from 108.21.194.27 at 17:09-17:11 UTC (a shared home address used by several staff, probably fine).

db-01 and ci-01: no compromise found. Recommended follow-up: review web-01 logs for 54.36.199.108 Nov 8-12 and what it could have read as the deploy account; move staff to SSH keys and disable password SSH; restrict Grafana to office/VPN; commit or remove the untracked inc/availability.php in the plugin.
